content_record.editorial_body: A new special issue reframes aging as a multi-system process driven by shared mechanisms—mitochondrial dysfunction, circadian disruption, hypoxia, and inter-organ signaling—with vascular and immune shifts as upstream drivers. Three things to remember - Mitochondrial dysfunction and circadian disruption are shared aging mechanisms. - Vascular and immune shifts drive tissue decline across organs. - Tissue microenvironments explain why aging trajectories differ. Source This signal is based on Aging as a Networked Process: Systems, Signals, and Interventions Across the Lifespan. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context. Health note: This editorial synthesizes 30 studies; specific biomarkers and interventions require further validation.
